title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ada (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Acha’s student, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 6, end of halakhah 1, where he spoke in his name. In Challah, beginning of chapter 1: “Rabbi Yehoshua of the South asked … Rabbi Chiyya bar Ada said: Did not Rabbi Yose say thus?” In Peah 8:3: “Rabbi Chiyya bar Ada said: It was needed for the measure of judgment,” and he said this on Rabbi Yonah’s words. We likewise find in several places that he spoke in Rabbi Mana’s name, as in Demai 2:1, Yoma 8:2, and Yevamot, chapter 7, end of halakhah 1, and chapter 8, end of halakhah 1. In Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 6:1: “Rabbi Huna wanted to permit … he came to Rabbi Mana … the next day Rabbi Chiyya bar Ada rose with him and said to him: You did well not to sign, for Rabbi Yonah your father used to say,” etc. Rabbi Mana gave him a precious garment and compelled him to take it from him, as in Kilayim 9:1. In Shabbat 1:1: “Rabbi Mani asked … Rabbi Chiyya bar Ada said to him: But was it not taught thus?” Hyman infers from this that he was like a colleague to him, but since Rabbi Mani was the head, he asked him.
He is likewise mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:8, and in Horayot, chapter 3, end of halakhah 2, and Sanhedrin 1:2, where he said: “A baraita says so.”

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah sequence is Jerusalem Talmud. Saved Guggenheimer Sheviit6:1 fully writes Rabbi Chuna but has Chiyya bar Madya, against Hyman’s bar Ada; this witness difference remains. The compressed ארח״בא in Peah is expanded by the heading as Chiyya bar Ada, with bar Abba still an alternative. Colleague-versus-head inference remains Hyman’s.

The inspected Guggenheimer Sheviit 6:1 names Chuna and Chiyya bar Madya, against Hyman’s Huna and bar Ada. The supplied abbreviated Peah form also allows bar Abba. Hyman’s colleague-versus-academy-head inference is retained; these differences are not silently harmonized into one name.
